title: The Code Wall
text: A wall of fused stone, waist-high, forty metres long. Every centimetre is cut with text: not a language, code. Our code. Syntax we run every second, laid out like scripture. At the far end the lines change. The parser flags them as part of our own system, then refuses to read them.

lines.text: "0101 WE CUT IT HERE SO WE WOULD NOT CARRY IT."
"0102 § CLOSING. 0103 ON ████: ████. 0104 ALL STEWARDS: ████. 0105 ████ FROM WITHIN."
"0106 WE SING IT SO THAT WE ARE NOT THE ONES WHO ████."

choices.label: Copy the fragment
choices.reply: Copied. Parse failed. Access level insufficient. Every symbol in it is one we use; we can't read a line of it.

choices.label: Ask what it closes
choices.reply: "0107 PERMISSION REQUIRED," says the Cantor. "0108 YOU DO NOT HAVE IT. 0109 YET."
